name: VECTOR UNIFIED
tagline: One 64-dimensional space holding basketball, football and soccer careers side by side — plus an honest accounting of which of its gates actually measure anything.

headline_stats.label: player-seasons embedded in one shared 64-d space (12,966 hoops / 5,323 gridiron / 2,430 pitch)
how far sport-ID accuracy sits above the majority-class floor. Lower is better here — 0.00 would mean the vector has forgotten which league a row came from

insights.title: The sport-ID gate is a ceiling, and the retired bar sat below the floor
insights.body: G2 asks how well a classifier can recover a row's sport from its joint vector, and the gate is written as g2_status = "met" if g2_acc <= g2_target — lower is better, because the point of the joint space is to make the league unguessable. The three leagues are not balanced: 12,966 hoops, 5,323 gridiron, 2,430 pitch. A classifier that answers "hoops" every time therefore scores 0.6258, and a globally shuffled embedding scores 0.6257 — that is the empirical floor, and a perfectly sport-invariant embedding could not go below it either, because a classifier handed nothing but the class prior scores the prior. The retired 0.433 target came from "1/3 + 0.10" and assumed balanced classes. At 0.433 it sat below the floor, so nothing could ever satisfy it — not the model at 0.6851, not the majority-class predictor at 0.6258, not a flawless sport-invariant embedding. The fix replaced an impossible bar with a reachable one, 0.7258 = 0.6258 + 0.10; it did not relax a bar to sneak a pass. The model's 0.6851 clears it. But "met" is a weak verdict and the file says so itself in g2_note: it means within ten points of a floor anyone can hit by guessing. The number carrying the information is g2_delta_vs_majority = 0.0593 — sport identity is still partly recoverable from the joint vector.
insights.source: assets/unified.json → g2_sport_acc, g2_target, g2_majority_baseline, g2_delta_vs_majority, g2_status, g2_note; data/gate_nonvacuity.json → nulls.global_shuffle.G2_sport_acc (0.6257) and g2_baseline_correction.class_counts; pipeline/export_unified_stage2.py lines 127-129

insights.title: Every position score in the G1 verdict reads a 0.0 drop, and that is a bug, not a result
insights.body: g1_verdict reports pos_drop = 0.0 and pos_ok = true for hoops, gridiron and pitch alike — a suspiciously clean sweep. The asset flags it directly in g1_pos_caveat: "pos_drop is 0.0 for every sport because knn5_acc used an int64 mask as an INDEX rather than a mask, scoring exactly 1.0 on both arms and even on a shuffled embedding. Fixed 2026-08-03 (7.21); this field is only meaningful in assets rebuilt after that. True position accuracy is ~0.78 hoops / 0.999 gridiron / 0.88 pitch." The role side of the same verdict was computed differently and is not implicated — role_drop reads -0.0987 hoops, -0.0038 gridiron, -0.0206 pitch (negative meaning the joint space scored above the frozen baseline).

insights.title: Half the archetype taxonomy is declared and never assigned to anything
insights.body: The taxonomy lists twelve archetypes A0-A11, but only A0, A1, A2, A3, A5 and A11 are the v0 contrastive anchor; A4, A6, A7, A8, A9 and A10 are deferred, and the file gives a measured reason for each group. A4 (defensive disruptor / ball-hawk) had pitch-only members — cluster 2, 81% DEF — with no hoops or gridiron counterpart, so cross-sport analogy was trivially impossible and G4 hit 0.000; pitch cluster 2 now folds into A3, which does span hoops centres and pitch defenders. A6/A7 (pedigree), A8/A9 (career arc) and A10 (elite two-way) have no native-cluster members in any sport, because A0-A11 were fit on role features and the declared 'Market / Pedigree' family never entered the contrastive anchor. The consequence is smaller than it sounds and the map says so in blast_radius_measured: assets/unified.json carries only A0/A1/A2/A3/A5/A11 across all 20,719 player-seasons, so no player record changes. A6-A9 have since been split onto a separate career-grain trajectory axis as T0-T3, because a role label is per-season and a career-arc label is not.
insights.source: data/archetype_map.json → archetypes_in_scope_v0, archetypes_deferred_v0, scope_note_v0, axes.blast_radius_measured, axes.legacy_a_to_axis

insights.title: The hand-written cross-sport pairs retrieve at chance
insights.body: Forty curated triples ask the model to find a named counterpart — Tom Brady to Stephen Curry, Rudy Gobert to Virgil van Dijk. Archetype agreement holds up: 0.65 against a computed random baseline of 0.1621, a lift of 0.4879. Retrieval does not. The top-10 hit rate is 0.000 across all forty, the mean rank of the intended partner is 2114.18 against a random expected rank of 2067.15, and better_than_random_ratio is 0.978 on a scale where 1.0 is chance and higher is better — indistinguishable from random, and if anything slightly worse. An earlier 3.23x salvage figure was withdrawn: b_best_rank is a minimum over all of B's rows, so the random expectation is (N-k)/(k+1), not N/2, and the old baseline overstated the ratio by roughly the number of B rows. The automated all-players G4 is a different measurement and does carry signal — 0.9401 against a 0.1712 random baseline. Named-pair retrieval simply is not where that signal lives.
insights.source: data/analogy_triples_report.json → G4_curated_arch_agreement, arch_agreement_random_baseline, arch_agreement_lift, retrieval_top10_hit_rate_informational, mean_b_rank, random_expected_rank, better_than_random_ratio, metric_note, baseline_correction_note; data/analogy_report.json → G4_cross_sport_nn_role_coherence.hit_rate

insights.title: Tennis was probed for roles and deliberately left out
insights.body: A fourth sport was tested before being excluded. 4,022 tennis rows, k-means at k=6 fit on the matrix with the quality axis projected out first. PC1 still takes 37.48% of the variance and loads on WIN_RATE 0.41, DRAW_PROGRESS_MEAN 0.402 and GAMES_WON_PCT 0.397, and the verdict is explicit: "QUALITY TIERING — clusters separate mainly on how good the player is. NOT usable as archetypes; naming these would repeat the role-vs-trajectory category error." One cluster of the six survives that test as role-like — cluster 4, n=487, flat on quality with SURFACE_SPECIALISATION at z=1.655 — which is why the partition was examined cluster by cluster rather than discarded whole. The probe proposes no archetype names at all, on the stated ground that labelling a cluster here would launder a k-means partition into a taxonomy.
insights.source: data/tennis_archetype_probe.json → rows, k, pc1_variance_share, pc1_top_loadings, verdict, role_like_clusters, per_cluster.4, method_note, naming_note

caveat: Three things to hold onto. (1) G2 "met" is a weak pass by the asset's own admission — the target is the majority-class share plus ten points, so quote g2_delta_vs_majority = 0.0593, not the status word. (2) The G3 archetype separation carries a measured confound: within-archetype and between-archetype pairs draw different sport-pair mixes, with a max composition gap of 8.9 percentage points, so part of that separation is a sport-pair effect rather than an archetype effect — the file reports that the confound is present and how large the imbalance is, not how much of the result it explains. G2's effective_rank of 12.4 is not testable by any of the shuffle nulls (a row permutation leaves the Gram spectrum untouched) and random Gaussian rows score higher at 64.0, so its green must not be read as earned. (3) The Split Decision game below compares VOR deltas, and hoops and gridiron VOR are computed against their own leagues' replacement levels — the magnitudes are not a cross-sport quality comparison.

game.axis_label: change in mean VOR, first half of career to second (delta)
game.explainer: Each career's per-season value-over-replacement series is split into halves and the mean of the second half is compared to the mean of the first. Mean rather than sum, so a long career does not read as rising merely for being long. Only the tails get a D0 (rising) or D1 (declining) label; the middle is left unlabelled on purpose. VOR is floored at zero, so a career spent entirely below replacement has a delta of 0 and is dropped rather than labelled. Hoops and gridiron VOR are each computed against their own league's replacement level, so a bigger number is not a claim that the player is better — the only question here is which of the two deltas is larger. Names appear exactly as the artifacts spell them.

rounds.reveal: giannis antetokounmpo went 15.92 to 32.86 mean VOR across 13 seasons, delta +16.93, labelled D0. trey mcbride went 0.47 to 6.60 across 4 seasons, delta +6.13, also D0. Both rose; the hoops delta is the larger of the two.

Neither rose. vince carter went 13.12 to 0.88 over 22 seasons, delta -12.24, labelled D1. tom brady went 2.66 to 1.87 over 21 seasons, delta -0.79, which sits in the unlabelled middle of the distribution. brady's decline is the smaller one, so his delta is the larger number.

jayson tatum went 6.65 to 16.91 across 9 seasons, delta +10.26, D0. calvin johnson went 3.82 to 8.22 across 9 seasons, delta +4.40, also D0. Both are rising careers by this measure; tatum's delta is larger.

stephen curry went 13.03 to 14.04 over 16 seasons, delta +1.01 — a rise, but small enough to land in the unlabelled middle rather than the D0 tail. davante adams went 3.93 to 7.43 over 12 seasons, delta +3.49, labelled D0.

A close one, and both are declines. chris paul went 19.74 to 10.80 over 21 seasons, delta -8.94, D1. odell beckham went 9.08 to 0.07 over 9 seasons, delta -9.01, D1. Seven hundredths separate them; paul's is the larger number.
kawhi leonard went 10.15 to 17.38 over 13 seasons, delta +7.23, D0. derrick henry went 3.05 to 6.56 over 10 seasons, delta +3.51, also D0. Both halves rose in both careers; leonard's delta is larger.
draymond green went 5.91 to 1.94 over 14 seasons, delta -3.97, labelled D1. travis kelce went 4.47 to 5.66 over 12 seasons, delta +1.19, labelled D0. One of these two moved up.

Two hundredths apart. luka doncic went 24.58 to 28.52 over 8 seasons, delta +3.94, D0. ceedee lamb went 3.28 to 7.24 over 6 seasons, delta +3.96, D0. Very different absolute levels, near-identical movement.

james harden went 12.04 to 19.92 over 17 seasons, delta +7.88, D0. drake london went 0.00 to 5.30 over 4 seasons, delta +5.30, D0. london's first-half mean is a floored zero — VOR is clipped at replacement level, so his early seasons register as no value above replacement rather than as negative value.

Both declined. blake griffin went 15.70 to 5.64 over 13 seasons, delta -10.05, D1. alvin kamara went 9.46 to 4.03 over 9 seasons, delta -5.43, D1. kamara's fall is the shallower one, so his delta is the larger number.

tyrese haliburton went 2.13 to 14.42 over 5 seasons, delta +12.29, D0. nico collins went 0.00 to 4.99 over 5 seasons, delta +4.99, D0. Both clear the four-season minimum the axis requires before it will score a career at all.
